body:
The reproducible evidence packet is now archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22834912 .

It includes the official 0.7.0 and 0.7.2 wheels, pinned source, the narrowly scoped candidate patch, regression tests, complete outputs and a portable replay script. ZIP SHA-256: `6be9658bd28e6bf72d9dac8add77319a703f4d6c7fedcacefee069604dfcc0a9`.

Readable report: https://www.gero.uz/research/articles/pyloan-explicit-payment-final-balloon.html

The packet retains the separate rounding differences and the unchanged upstream test failures; it does not claim an accepted fix or a green full suite. The earlier automatic-amortization correction remains credited. This comment adds archival links to this existing report, not a new issue.

Version 1.1 evidence addendum: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22836495 . A small published GERO adapter now follows the same final schedule row through a synthetic payment notice and an example budget check. The notice requests 919.10 instead of 100; with a budget of 150, the check changes from WITHIN_BUDGET to EXCEEDS_BUDGET (769.10 above budget). The candidate restores both outputs, and restoration reproduces both differences.

The adapter is demonstration code, not a built-in PyLoan feature or a tested bank integration. This is accelerated principal in the schedule, not measured fees, extra interest or borrower losses; no payment was collected. The original 864-case audit and its limitations are unchanged. The addendum includes all five sets of generated documents and a portable replay; SHA-256 `63e6b8dcc6d7bb2b3ed1179897e869b87a9754392b8099b1dcb0e4fc567010cf`.

@kadyrbekovhamit-cyber: Thank you for the incredibly thorough bug report, the clear reproduction steps, and the exact candidate fix.

You were absolutely right—the final payment override introduced to handle automatically sized loans was improperly catching explicitly sized annuities. I have implemented your suggested guard to ensure that `LoanType.ANNUITY` loans with a user-provided `payment_amount` bypass the balance-clearing step, allowing the residual balance to remain. I also added a dedicated regression test based on your reproduction code to ensure this behavior remains stable going forward.

This fix has been merged and is now live in **PyLoan v0.7.3**. You can pull the latest version from PyPI:

```bash
pip install --upgrade pyloan

```

Thanks again for your excellent contribution and for making it so easy to track down and resolve! Please feel free to reach out if you notice any further issues.
